content.user_title: Plan Agile Releases with Sprint Roadmaps
content.value_statement: Release planning often breaks down when timelines, tasks, and dependencies are scattered. This skill turns project context into sprint schedules, task codes, milestones, and roadmap views.
actual_capabilities: Creates sprint schedules with sequential SPRINT-001 codes.
Breaks work into task tickets using T-001 numbering.
Maps sprints into monthly, quarterly, or phase-based roadmaps.
Adds dependencies, milestones, and release checkpoints.
Applies capacity guidance such as 80 percent planning buffers.
Provides reusable release plan templates and example formats.
limitations: Does not estimate effort from live team history unless the user provides velocity data.
Does not connect to Jira, GitHub, or project management tools.
Does not replace product prioritization or stakeholder approval.
Uses planning guidance only; it does not execute project work.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Release
use_cases.description: Turn scope, timeline, and team size into a sprint plan with milestones and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Engineering Delivery
use_cases.description: Break implementation work into coded tasks that teams can discuss during sprint planning.

use_cases.title: Communicate a Roadmap
use_cases.description: Summarize upcoming sprint outcomes by month, quarter, or project phase for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Release Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agile release plan for [project]. Timeline: [duration]. Team: [team size]. Include sprints, task codes, dependencies, and milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Backlog Into Sprints
prompt_templates.scenario: Organizing known features into delivery work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this backlog into two-week sprints with SPRINT-001 and T-001 codes: [backlog]. Show dependencies and release checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Stakeholder Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Creating a roadmap view from planned work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a roadmap for [release name] using these priorities: [priorities]. Group sprints by month and highlight alpha, beta, and production milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Adjust for Risk and Capacity
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with constraints and dependencies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this release plan for a team of [team size] with [capacity constraints]. Front-load risky work and add a buffer sprint.

output_examples.input: Plan an eight-week mobile app MVP for two developers.
output_examples.output: A four-sprint release plan with user foundation, activity tracking, visualization, and launch preparation phases.

output_examples.input: Create a six-sprint checkout release roadmap for an e-commerce platform.
output_examples.output: A quarterly roadmap with payment foundation, checkout UI, payment integration, testing, beta launch, and production release.

output_examples.input: Break this backlog into sprints and show dependencies.
output_examples.output: A sprint schedule with unique task codes, dependency notes, milestones, and a stakeholder-friendly roadmap summary.

best_practices: Provide scope, timeline, team size, and priorities before asking for a plan.
Review dependencies and milestones with delivery leads before sharing the roadmap.
Keep task codes stable after publication so teams can discuss work consistently.
anti_patterns: Asking for a plan without timeline or team capacity.
Treating generated dates as commitments before team review.
Using the skill to replace backlog grooming or product discovery.

faq.question: Will this skill create Jira tickets?
faq.answer: No. It creates planned task codes and descriptions that you can copy into project tools.

faq.question: Can it handle short and long releases?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include short release templates and longer release patterns with phases.

faq.question: Does it create unique sprint and task codes?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses sequential sprint codes and task codes across the full release.

faq.question: Can I provide my own dates?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide start dates, milestone dates, or sprint duration so the plan fits your calendar.

faq.question: Will it estimate capacity automatically?
faq.answer: It can apply simple capacity guidance when you provide team size, sprint length, and constraints.

faq.question: Should I include confidential roadmap details?
faq.answer: Only include sensitive plans if your AI environment is approved for that information.
